newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S GARDENIA GETS CLEARANCE TO LIST SHARES.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S GARDENIA GETS CLEARANCE TO LIST SHARES.

text.p: Hungarian curtain factory Gardenia Rt received a go-ahead from the Budapest Stock Exchange's council on Monday to list its shares, company officials told a news conference on Tuesday.
"We're aware of the fact the bourse council made a positive judgment so we have a good chance to appear (on the market)," Peter Zelnik, chairman of Gardenia's supervisory board said.

Gardenia, ahead of a combined capital market transaction which would include the sale of own shares and the issue of new shares, expects trading to start in its shares in April in the listed "A" category of the bourse.

Details of the planned transaction were published on Monday. The company will sell 222,000 own shares and will issue 400,000 new shares, all with 500 forint face value, at 1,465 forints/share subscription price during the subscription period which will run between March 10 and 21.
After the issue of the new shares Gardenia's one billion forint share capital would rise to 1.2 billion forints.
The transaction, guaranteed by lead manager Hofmann Schneider Securities and participating MKB Securities, will allow Gardenia to raise 911 million forints, Gardenia said in a statement.
The money will be spent on new investments and acquisition.
"We've always had many more ideas than what we could have afforded to finance," Chairwoman and General Director Marta Polyak said. "This is the situation now, too."
Since 1995 Gardenia has been implementing an intensive investment programme under which it plans to complete a new knitting plant this year.
The company's acquisition plans focus on home textiles and would strengthen Gardenia's position in the central European region as most of its exports go to west Europe.
"Our target is to become the leading home textile company of central and eastern Europe," Istvan Schmidt, Gardenia's deputy General Director said.
Gardenia's exports account for a bigger part than domestic sales within the company's total sales.

"According to Gardenia's opinion these (central and eastern European) markets could expect a bigger growth than west Eujrope as the projected economic recovery could boost the currently restricted power of purchase," Gardenia's share issue prospectus said.

According to preliminary unconsolidated HAS figures Gardenia's sales rose to 3.1 billion forints in 1996 from 2.96 billion in 1995, with exports accounting for 1.77 billion last year. Its after-tax profit was 303 million in 1996 compared to 440 million in 1995.

As to the lead manager, Gardenia's deal will be Hofmann Schneider's second transaction after organising the share issue and bourse listing of research and development company Horizon-Multiplan in 1996.
Herbert Werner, Hofmann Schneider's managing director said the securities house plans to organise four more IPOs this year.
As to participating MKB Securities, deputy General Director Laszlo Viragh said Gardenia has been the client of MKB Bank, which is the sole owner of MKB securities house.
"The company (Gardenia) and our bank have been cooperating for years and we regarded it as natural to participate in such an important step of a company's life as going public," Viragh said.
